subject: impute missing variable thats also being used as an index for random intercept

messages.author: 8aaac405ce0daa2d
messages.subject: impute missing variable thats also being used as an index for random intercept
parts:
Hi,


  • I want to impute missing values of a variable "hh" 
    • This variable is integer type and ranges (0,5)
  • I am using this variable to index random intercepts for each value in a likeilhood.
    • a_hh[hh[i]+1]
To get the rest of the model working, I imputed missing values with the mode value, but now I want to do the imputation within the nimble model.

A toy version of the code is below:

toy_impute <- nimbleCode({
  
  # hyperpriors for sd of random intercepts
  sigma_zip ~ T(dnorm(mean = 0, sd = coef_prior_scale), min = 0) # zip code
  sigma_hh ~ T(dnorm(mean = 0, sd = coef_prior_scale), min = 0) # hh
  
  # random intercepts
  for(i in 1:N_zip){ a_zip[i] ~ dnorm(mean = 0, sd = sigma_zip) }
  for(i in 1:6){ a_hh[i] ~ dnorm(mean = 0, sd = sigma_hh) }
  
  # coefficient priors
  b[2] ~ dnorm(mean = 0, sd = coef_prior_scale)
  b[3] ~ dnorm(mean = 0, sd = coef_prior_scale / sd(x_zip[]))
  g[1] ~ dnorm(mean = 0, sd = coef_prior_scale)

  # prior on centered intercept
  b[1] ~ dlogis(location = 0 - b[2]*mean(male[]) - b[3]*mean(x_zip[]), scale = 1)
  
  for(i in 1:N){
    # likelihood
    y[i] ~ dpois(lambda[i])
    log(lambda[i]) <- log(n[i]) + b[1] + b[2]*male[i] + b[3]*x_zip[i] + 
      a_zip[zip[i]] + a_hh[hh[i]+1] 
    
    # imputation missing hh[i]
    hh[i] ~ dpois(lambda_hh[i])
    log(lambda_hh[i]) <- g[1] #+ g[2]*male[i] + g[3]*x_xip[i]
    #constraint_data ~ dconstraint(hh[i] <= 6)
  }
})


I get the following error when compiling: 
  • Warning: dynamic index out of bounds: exp(log_oPn_oBi_cB_cP + b[1] + b[2] * male_oBi_cB + b[3] * x_zip_oBi_cB + a_zip[zip_oBi_cB] + a_hh[hh[i]] 

I think the issue is that I can't use a dynamic index in the likelihood. I also tried assigning hh[i] to another variable, that resulted in the same error. Also, I think the issue may be that I need a constraint on the imputed values so they stay within the (1,6) range. If so is there an easy way to do that (e.g.: constraint_data ~ dconstraint(hh[i] <= 6))

Thanks,

Cam

messages.author: 5fa2a363d4ddd1d1
messages.subject: Re: impute missing variable thats also being used as an index for random intercept
parts:
Hi Cam,

Yes, you need to ensure that "hh[1]+1" gives a value that is a legitimate index for a "a_hh" in all cases. This could either be through the priors on each element of hh or via using dconstraint.  One possibility for the prior is to keep using the Poisson but to truncate it. The nimble manual (Section 5.2.7) has information on truncation and on use of dconstraint.

-chris

messages.author: 5fa2a363d4ddd1d1
messages.subject: Re: impute missing variable thats also being used as an index for random intercept
parts:
Oh, also, your use of dconstraint is not quite right. You either need to use constraint_data[i], one for each constraint, or, outside of the loop, to have a single dconstraint and use boolean operations, such as constraint_data  ~ dconstraint(hh[1] <= 6 && hh[2] <= 6 && hh[3] <= 6 && ....). The latter of course is tedious with large N. 

Finally, it's possible that even with a correctly specified prior or constraint, you may still see warnings about a dynamic index out of bounds, if nimble tries to use a proposed index that is invalid in the course of the MCMC sampler assigned to the hh[i] nodes. An invalid proposal will be rejected, and correctly so, but the issue is just whether a_hh[hh[i]+1 is evaluated during the course of the sampler. This may depend on the exact sampler used, and I think use of the truncation approach is more likely to avoid this. Feel free to follow up if you run into questions on this front.
